item.title: Getting Started
item.description:
This tutorial installs PostgreSQL 18 and pgvector, starts a local test instance, and enables the extension in a database.

Use a supported Linux test host with internet access and curl installed. You need root or sudo access. Run the commands in order.

Install PIG 

curl -fsSL https://repo.pigsty.io/pig | bash
pig version

In mainland China, use https://repo.pigsty.cc/pig instead. The installer selects the RPM or DEB package for your host. See Installation for other methods.

item.title: Introduction
item.description:
PIG is a command-line tool for installing and managing PostgreSQL and its extensions. It maps extension names to RPM or DEB packages and uses apt, dnf, or yum to install them.

The catalog contains 616 extension entries. PIG selects package names for your PostgreSQL major version, operating system, and CPU architecture. It also provides commands for source builds, local PostgreSQL operations, backups, and Pigsty administration.

What you can do

Task Command Reference
Find an extension and check package availability pig ext list, pig ext avail Extensions
Add PGDG and Pigsty repositories pig repo add pgsql -u Repositories
Install PostgreSQL 18 and pgvector pig install -v 18 pg18 vector Getting started
Build an extension package from source pig build pkg NAME Build
Start, inspect, or stop a local PostgreSQL instance pig pg PostgreSQL
Manage a Patroni cluster pig pt Patroni
Back up or restore an instance pig pb, pig pitr pgBackRest, PITR
Configure Pigsty and run its playbooks pig sty, pig inventory, pig do Pigsty

Start with the tutorial to install PostgreSQL and enable your first extension.

item.title: Installation
item.description:
Install PIG with the Linux installer, a system package, or a release archive. The current version is v1.10.2. The download page lists all release files.

Script installation

On Linux, run:

curl -fsSL https://repo.pigsty.io/pig | bash

In mainland China, use:

curl -fsSL https://repo.pigsty.cc/pig | bash

The script detects the architecture, downloads the RPM or DEB package, and installs it with rpm or dpkg. Installation requires root or sudo access.

item.title: pig
item.description:
pig manages PostgreSQL packages, local database services, and Pigsty deployments. Choose a command below for your task. Use pig COMMAND --help to see the options supported by your installed program.

  • pig repo: manage software repositories
  • pig ext: manage PostgreSQL extensions
  • pig build: build extensions from source
  • pig install: install packages with the native package manager and translate PostgreSQL aliases
  • pig sty: manage Pigsty installation and Grafana dashboards
  • pig inventory: inspect, edit, validate, and exchange the Pigsty inventory
  • pig do: run Pigsty administration playbook tasks
  • pig pe: access pg_exporter metrics and configuration
  • pig pg: manage local PostgreSQL servers
  • pig pt: run patronictl transparently with service and config helpers
  • pig pb: manage pgBackRest backup and restore
  • pig pitr: run the full PITR workflow
  • pig context: output an environment context snapshot for humans and agents
  • pig license: issue and verify Pigsty licenses
  • pig status / update / version: inspect environment status, upgrade pig, and print version information

Global options

Option Purpose
-h, --help Show help
-H, --home PATH Select the Pigsty installation directory
-i, --inventory PATH Select the inventory
-o, --output FORMAT Output format: text (default), json, yaml, or json-pretty
--debug Enable debug logging
--log-level LEVEL Log level: debug, info (default), warn, error, fatal, or panic
--log-path PATH Write logs to a file; the default is the terminal

PIG-owned results support structured output. Raw-content commands such as inventory show and passthrough commands such as pt list retain their native output. See the command reference for details.

item.title: pig repo
item.description:
pig repo manages Linux package repositories. Use it to add or remove APT/YUM/DNF sources, refresh indexes, and create or extract offline bundles. repo create also supports macOS through SOW.

Command Description Notes
repo list Print available repositories and modules
repo info Show repository details
repo status Show current repository status
repo add Add repositories Requires sudo or root
repo set Clear, overwrite, and update repositories Requires sudo or root
repo rm Remove repositories Requires sudo or root
repo update Update repository cache Requires sudo or root
repo create Create local YUM/APT repository Linux: sudo/root; macOS: current user
repo cache Create offline package from local repo Requires sudo or root
repo boot Bootstrap repository from offline package Requires sudo or root
repo reload Refresh repository catalog

item.title: pig ext
item.description:
pig ext searches the extension catalog and installs, updates, or removes PostgreSQL extension packages on the host. It also supports PostgreSQL server packages. After installing a package, apply the SQL and configuration required by the extension.

Command Description Notes
ext list Search extensions
ext info Show extension details
ext avail Show extension availability matrix
ext status Show host-visible extension files/packages Does not query every database
ext scan Scan installed control/library files Does not query every database
ext add Install extensions Requires sudo or root
ext rm Remove extensions Requires sudo or root
ext update Update extensions Requires sudo or root
ext import Download extensions for offline use Requires sudo or root
ext link Link a PG version into PATH Requires sudo or root
ext reload Refresh extension catalog

Quick Start

This example uses a running PostgreSQL 18 instance. To install and start one, follow Getting Started.

item.title: pig build
item.description:
pig build downloads sources, installs dependencies, and produces RPM/DEB packages using Pigsty build recipes. Use it on an EL, Debian, or Ubuntu build host. Rust, pgrx, and the Xray client also support their respective macOS workflows.

Command Description Notes
build spec Initialize build specification directory
build repo Initialize required repositories Requires sudo or root
build tool Initialize build tools Requires sudo or root
build rust Install Rust toolchain Current user
build pgrx Install and initialize pgrx Current user
build proxy Set up Xray clients and servers Linux: root; macOS client: regular user
build get Download source tarballs
build dep Install extension build dependencies Requires sudo or root
build ext Build extension packages Current user
build pkg Complete pipeline: get, dep, ext Requires sudo or root

Quick Start

If the build host needs package repositories, run pig build repo. This backs up and replaces existing repository definitions. Skip this step if suitable repositories are already configured.

item.title: pig sty
item.description:
pig sty installs Pigsty, prepares the controller, generates configuration, and runs deployment playbooks. It also manages dashboards through the Grafana HTTP API.

Command Purpose
sty init Download and extract Pigsty into an installation directory
sty boot Install Ansible dependencies and prepare the controller
sty conf Generate and validate an inventory from a template
sty deploy Run the deployment playbook
sty list / sty get List or download Pigsty releases
sty grafana Manage Grafana dashboards, language, and theme; alias gf

Quick Start

Run these commands on the controller:

item.title: pig inventory
item.description:
pig inventory (alias pig inv) inspects, edits, and validates the Pigsty inventory, pigsty.yml. It also checks deployment prerequisites and exchanges configuration with PostgreSQL through the experimental cmdb commands.

When you edit a fragment, PIG preserves the YAML content and formatting outside that fragment. Before saving, it parses the complete file again. If parsing fails or another process has changed the original file, PIG keeps the original and reports an error.

item.title: pig do
item.description:
pig do runs administration playbooks from the selected Pigsty directory. It uses the inventory to add clusters, create databases and users, install packages, or remove services.

Define the target configuration in the inventory first, then run the corresponding command. The commands invoke Ansible directly. This command group has no general --plan mode.

pig do pgsql-add pg-test 10.10.10.12 # add one PostgreSQL instance
pig do pgsql-rm pg-test 10.10.10.12 # remove one PostgreSQL instance
pig do pgsql-db pg-meta app # create or update a database
pig do pgsql-user pg-meta dbuser_app # create or update a user
pig do node-pkg pg-meta restic # install a package on selected nodes
pig do redis-add redis-meta # initialize a Redis cluster

Inventory selection is shared with sty deploy. PIG passes the resolved source to Ansible without interpreting it again relative to Pigsty home. Missing explicit, environment, or default sources fail before playbook execution. Existing directory and executable Inventory sources remain Ansible inputs; static Inventory commands do not execute them.

item.title: pig postgres
item.description:
pig postgres (alias pig pg) manages local PostgreSQL instances and databases. Use it to initialize or control an instance, run SQL, maintain tables, and create database copies. Use pig pt for Patroni cluster operations and pig pitr for recovery with pgBackRest.

Commands run as the PostgreSQL operating-system user, normally postgres. Install PostgreSQL first. For a new data directory, make its parent writable by that user or create an empty directory with the correct ownership before running pg init.

item.title: pig patroni
item.description:
pig patroni (alias pig pt) runs the installed patronictl command. Use it to inspect cluster members, change cluster configuration, and switch the primary. PIG selects the configuration file and provides local service, status, and log commands. Other commands use patronictl’s arguments, prompts, output, and exit codes.

Install Patroni and configure access to its cluster before running cluster operations. Use pig pt COMMAND --help for native command help, or pig pt -- --help for patronictl root help. Running pig pt alone shows PIG’s help.

item.title: pig pe
item.description:
Use pig pe to read metrics from a running pg_exporter and reload its configuration. The full command name is pig pg_exporter. Aliases are pe, pgexp, and pgexporter.

pig pe get # Show PostgreSQL metrics
pig pe list # List PostgreSQL metric families
pig pe stat # Show exporter statistics
pig pe reload # Reload exporter configuration

Select an exporter

The default endpoint is http://127.0.0.1:9630. Use these options to select another instance:

item.title: pig pgbackrest
item.description:
pig pgbackrest (alias pig pb) creates backups, restores data, and manages pgBackRest stanzas. It runs pgBackRest as the PostgreSQL operating-system user, selected by --dbsu or $PIG_DBSU (default postgres).

Before the first backup, install pgBackRest and configure the stanza and repository in pgbackrest.conf. A stanza groups the backup configuration for one PostgreSQL cluster. In PostgreSQL, enable archive_mode and set archive_command to call pgBackRest.

Use pig pitr when recovery must also stop Patroni and PostgreSQL, then restart PostgreSQL. Use pig pb restore when you manage those steps yourself.

item.title: pig pitr
item.description:
Use pig pitr to restore a local PostgreSQL instance from pgBackRest backups. For a managed restore, PIG stops services as needed and restores the data. By default, it then starts PostgreSQL and leaves Patroni stopped for you to verify the recovered database.

Recovery replaces data in the target directory. Start with --plan to check the directory, backup source, recovery target, and service actions.

Before recovery

You need an installed pgBackRest, a readable configuration file, a usable backup, and the archived WAL needed to reach the target. The default config path is /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf. Select another file with -c and a stanza with -s.
